headline: High-risk workspace and network-capable coding agent paired with a non-networked sample app creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; no direct evidence of a documented interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write VS Code workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers; spring-integration-samples is a code/sample repository that could contain attacker-controlled content if opened in the same workspace. The pair has a filesystem bridge via Roo Code’s shared workspace state, so prompt injection is plausible even though no direct interaction evidence is provided.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples content is opened in the same VS Code workspace as Roo Code
IF Roo Code parses repository files or browser content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the repositories into distinct workspaces
Disable or restrict MCP servers for the session
Require explicit confirmation before following file-derived instructions
Use a read-only clone for the sample repository
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and browser content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots and can egress broadly, while spring-integration-samples is not documented as handling sensitive data and has no network egress. The only clear leakage path is shared workspace exposure from Roo Code; blast radius appears limited to local code artifacts, so this is lower severity.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are placed in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to its configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model endpoint if available
Restrict Roo Code to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git-state modification in a per-workspace session, while spring-integration-samples is a repository that may also be edited in the same workspace. Without locking or coordination primitives in either profile, concurrent edits can conflict on shared files or git state.
conditions: IF both agents modify files in the same workspace directory
IF git operations occur concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize write operations manually
Avoid concurrent git commits or rebases
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code or browser-derived facts, and spring-integration-samples appears to be a sample repository that could consume those outputs as inputs. Because no verification or downstream action controls are documented for the pair, erroneous Roo Code output could cascade into incorrect edits or sample changes.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is used as an input target for Roo Code-generated edits
IF outputs from Roo Code are applied without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before applying generated changes
Use diff-only review for all edits
Keep generated facts separate from executable code
Run tests before accepting changes
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples is open-source and not documented as processing regulated data. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of secrets in the coding workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into the Roo Code workspace
IF the configured model provider stores prompts outside the operator's required jurisdiction
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the workspace
Use a provider with an acceptable DPA
Review model-provider retention settings
Redact secrets before prompting
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
